items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENERGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENERGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4303

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public service law, in relation to farm waste net
energy metering


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This legislation amends section 66-j of Public Service law to ensure
more equitable net metering provisions for owners of farm-based
anaerobic or manure digesters in New York State.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section 66-j of the Public Service law is amended to:

* Amends subsection 1-e the definition of "farm waste electric
generating equipment" to increase the allowable rated capacity to not
more than one thousand kilowatts.

* Adds a new subsection 2-a to allow owners of anaerobic digester to
own any environment attributes and provide such owners the ability to
grant ownership of these attributes to other entities.

* Amends subsection 4-c, (ii) to reduce the rate paid by owners or
operators of anaerobic digesters for grid connection from $5,000 to
$3,000 per farm operation.

* Adds a new subsection 5-e to allow eligible credits sustained from
net metering activity from farm anaerobic digesters be applied against
electricity use from all grid connections on the farm operation.

 JUSTIFICATION :
This legislation would make needed amendments to net metering laws as
adopted by New York State during the 2008 Legislative Session for
anaerobic digesters.  These digesters are mostly located on dairy
farms where methane from manure is captured and used to produce
electricity on the farm and, in many cases, net metered back to the
grid for use by others.

The 2008 net-metering law further encourages the development of behind
the meter renewable energy sources. These changes were designed to
further incentivize the development of renewable energy sources that
individual ratepayers would construct.  This helps increase the amount
of renewable energy available in New York and reduce our dependence on
fossil fuels. However, there are a number of issues that need to be
addressed as a result of the passage of this legislation to ensure
that the digester technology is treated equitably, when compared to
solar and wind technologies. This bill seeks to make these changes,
including expansion of the amount of energy that can be net metered
for anaerobic digesters. By addressing these issues, this legislation
improves the state's positive net-metering law for this farm-specific
renewable energy technology and provides both benefits for the
environment and renewable energy production.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become law.
